verdict.rationale: The product has a public GitHub repository (Proa-Labs/proa) whose README content is quoted, and `proa ui add` vendors component source into the user's repo to own and edit, so the source appears readable. No evidence states the license, so the 'open license' half of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license (e.g. MIT/Apache) for the core framework, and confirmation that the full framework source, not just a README and vendored UI components, is publicly browsable.
